name: Annual Tax Demand Notice
summary: An assessment from the Tax Authority of how much you owe (or are owed) for a given tax year, with a payment or appeal deadline.

guidance.primaryNextStep: Compare the reported income and amount due against your own records before you decide whether to pay or appeal.
guidance.deadlineSummary: Date shown on the notice (typically 30 days)
guidance.appliesWhen: the Tax Authority says you owe money or need to respond about a specific tax year
guidance.recommendedChannel: Use the payment or objection channel printed on the notice and keep proof of every submission.
guidance.whenToContactAuthority: the income, amount due, or deadline does not match your records
guidance.whatToVerify: Verify the tax year, reported income, total amount due, and the final payment or objection deadline.

sections.explainer: Tax year — the calendar year this demand relates to. In Israel the tax year matches the calendar year (January through December).
Reported income — the income figure on which the tax was calculated. This is based on your or your employer's filings (Form 106 from your employer is the most common source).
sections.actionRequired: Compare this figure against your own records. If it's wrong, you can dispute the demand within 30 days.

sections.explainer: Amount owed — the total tax due, often including penalties and interest (ribit) on any underpayment. A negative amount means you're owed a refund.
Payment deadline — pay by this date to avoid additional interest charges and to keep the case out of enforcement (hotza'a la-po'al).
sections.actionRequired: Pay via Bank HaPoalim / online banking / the Tax Authority website. Keep proof of payment.
sections.deadline: Date shown on the notice (typically 30 days)

sections.explainer: How to appeal — if you disagree with the calculation, file a written objection (erur) within 30 days of receiving the notice. State the tax year, case number, and the specific item you're disputing.
sections.actionRequired: If the amount is large, consider consulting an accountant (ro'eh cheshbon) before submitting the appeal.
